Verifier notes and special checks

One page holds five systems and twenty-five printed regions. System 1 opens in treble and bass with two sharps and 2/4, then one eighth-note pickup. The remaining twenty-four regions are complete bars in 2/4. No clef change, key change, meter change, repeat, or ending is printed; the same two clefs and two sharps are reprinted at the start of systems 2, 3, 4, and 5. Each system ends with a barline, so no bar is split across a system break. The last region closes with a thin-thick final barline, and D.C. is printed under the bass staff. Systems 2, 3, and 4 were already frozen and are copied unchanged. The movement title sits above the system 1 crop and is not cut; notes, slurs, dynamics, the ritardando text, D.C., and the closing barline stay inside their crops.

  • System 1, first region: Is the opening region a full bar? No. After the treble and bass clefs, two sharps, and the 2/4 sign, the upper staff has one flagged eighth note and the lower staff has one eighth rest.
  • System 5, last region: Is the closing thin-thick barline an end repeat? No. A thin stroke and a thick stroke close the bar, and no repeat dots are printed in the staff spaces beside them. D.C. is printed under the bass staff.
  • Ends of all five systems: Does any system end without a barline, so that its last bar continues on the next system? No. Each system ends with a barline through both staves, so no region is split.
